planned_adaptations.Cognition & Learning: Use four large, numbered spaces. Show one action at a time, then fade the pointing prompt. Repeat the same slow count. Return to four even taps before adding a rest.
planned_adaptations.Communication & Interaction: Teach the words with a tap, a quiet open hand and a picture. Accept a nod, sign, point, gesture or a short phrase. Give wait time and check the pupil has chosen the role.
planned_adaptations.SEMH: Use a calm sound level, predictable start and stop cues, paired practice and a private response option. A pupil may pause, watch a round, then rejoin on the next count-in.
planned_adaptations.Sensory/Physical: Offer soft finger taps, a nod, a pointer or a single comfortable movement. Position the beat strip within reach and sight. Sound is optional; accurate timed movement counts.
planned_adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pair each key word with the same action and symbol. Model a short stem, then invite the pupil to use words, a sign or a demonstration.

title: Keep four even beats
goal: I can keep a steady beat and leave a quiet rest.
status: Practice for the Week 2 outcome. Observe each pupil keeping four even beat spaces, including rests. Keep only a real record of the pupil’s attempt. This lesson alone does not complete the award.
success: I can leave the same gap from beat to beat.
I can keep a rest quiet for one whole beat.
I can start and stop with a cue.
words: The even pulse you can tap or show.
The beat keeps the same speed.
A quiet beat. Keep its space in time.
A count that tells us when to start.
steps: Watch the count-in: one, two, three, four.
Tap once in each numbered space. Keep it even.
At REST, stay quiet for one whole beat.
Try it again. Are the gaps still the same?
demo: Point to four numbered spaces. Give four slow, even counts without playing. Say: “This is the count-in. We start on the next one.”
Play A: TAP, TAP, TAP, TAP. Move the pointer through spaces 1–4 at the same rate. Say: “One tap in each space. My gaps stay the same.”
Play B: TAP, REST, TAP, REST. Keep the pointer moving through all four spaces. Say: “A rest is quiet. Beat two still takes one full space.”
Repeat B twice after a fresh four-count. Show the raised-hand stop cue. Say: “I keep the spaces even. I stop at the cue.” Let a pupil show beat two without a sound.
mistakes: The pupil speeds up after a rest
Keep the pointer moving through every numbered space. Say “tap, wait, tap, wait” at one pace. Practise B with a visible nod for every beat, then fade the nod.
The pupil skips a rest and starts the next tap early
Point to beat two and count its full length. Contrast TAP REST TAP REST with TAP TAP. Both rests need a place. Return to four even taps, then put the rests back.
A louder tap is treated as a better beat
Use soft taps or silent movements at the same pace. Praise timing, not loudness. Return to the agreed low sound level and stop cue.

setup: Place four numbered spaces where every pupil can see them. Check the soft tapping option and agree the flat-hand STOP cue. Keep the room quiet. Use a pair and a trio; rotate beat keeper, player and watcher. Give each pupil a strip and a personal response record. Model with original class parts only. Do not use commercial music or external media.
cleanup: At 34 minutes, invite each pupil to try B once and choose one next step. Record the actual timing and prompt used. Ask the pupil to check the scribed comment. Return cards and mats; leave the next part strip ready for the second lesson. Put the selected pupil record at A page 1.
end_question: How do you keep the beat when the part is quiet?

starter_answer: B. Beats two and four are full quiet rests. A and B both keep the same four even beat spaces. Do not treat B as unsteady because it has fewer sounds.

timing: Arrival
Choose a quiet movement, teach STOP and retrieve four numbered spaces.
Starter
Compare A and B. Find the quiet rests in B; both parts last four even beats.
I do
Use the 60-second model; rehearse count-in, pulse and full rests; check after modelling.
We do
Play A together for four minutes; play B and use the hinge for four minutes.
You do
22–28 choose and practise one route; 28–34 try, receive one next step and retry; 34–37 record, check and tidy.
Exit
Each pupil shows one attempt or explains a rest; record actual support.
cfu: After I do, point to beat two in B. Ask: “Tap or quiet?” Each pupil shows quiet, then points to beat three on the next beat. If the pupil skips straight to three, repeat a slow model with a pointer.
hinge: At We do 2, show B: TAP REST TAP REST. Ask: “Does beat two still take time?” Choose A: no time, or B: one full quiet beat. Correct B. parallel_hinge: Retest with REST TAP REST TAP. Ask: “What happens on beat one?” Correct: a full quiet beat; play on two. Check with a visible pointer rather than a verbal guess alone.

title: Join our group part
goal: I can join a group part and keep the beat.
status: Second practice lesson for the Week 2 outcome. Group playing is a classroom practice task. Observe each learner’s own entry, rests, repeat and stop; do not infer that a wider event or the award has been completed.
success: I can start after a clear count-in.
I can keep my part for two rounds.
I can watch the cue and stop with the group.
words: The bit each player does in the group.
A sign that tells us what to do.
The even beat that goes on under a part.
steps: Choose A or B. Keep your own four spaces.
Watch the count-in. Start on the next one.
Play your part twice. Keep every rest.
Watch the flat hand. Stop with the group.
demo: Place A and B side by side with aligned beat numbers. Say: “A taps on all four beats. B taps on one and three. Each line lasts four beats.”
Give a four-count. Use one hand to tap A and point through B with the other, or ask a second adult to play B. Keep the volume low. Say: “We use the same pulse.”
Play both lines for two rounds. Count beat positions aloud at first, then fade the count. Say: “B is quiet on two and four, but the beat goes on.”
Show a flat hand after the second round and stop. Model a missed entry, wait for a new count-in, then start again. Say: “If I lose my place, I watch, wait and rejoin at the next one.”
mistakes: The pupil copies the other part and loses their own
Return to the pupil’s A or B strip. Ask for a point through it while a partner plays. Add the pupil’s movement only after a new count-in.
A pupil tries to catch up with fast taps
Stop gently. Say “watch, wait, next one”. Give a fresh four-count and start a new round. Do not fill the missing beats with extra taps.
The group ends at different times
Agree two rounds before starting. Count the rounds with two fingers and show the flat hand at the end of round two. Fade extra cues when pupils are ready.

setup: Retrieve each pupil’s first attempt and next step from lesson one. Set A and B under the same numbered beat row. Practise STOP before starting. Keep the volume low and confirm the quiet option.
cleanup: Use minutes 34–37 to play the last checked two-round attempt, capture one personal comment and note the actual support. Let pupils confirm scribed words. Store the chosen record at A page 2; update only actual evidence. Return cards and mats. Keep the next aim available for later rehearsals.

starter: A and B both use four even beat spaces. Do they last the same time?
starter_answer: Yes, if each beat space stays even. A has four sounds. B has two sounds and two rests, all with the same full beat length. Both end after four beats.

lines: Choose A or B. Keep your own four spaces.

slides.notes: 0–15 seconds Place A and B side by side with aligned beat numbers. Say: “A taps on all four beats. B taps on one and three. Each line lasts four beats.” 15–30 seconds Give a four-count. Use one hand to tap A and point through B with the other, or ask a second adult to play B. Keep the volume low. Say: “We use the same pulse.” 30–45 seconds Play both lines for two rounds. Count beat positions aloud at first, then fade the count. Say: “B is quiet on two and four, but the beat goes on.” 45–60 seconds Show a flat hand after the second round and stop. Model a missed entry, wait for a new count-in, then start again. Say: “If I lose my place, I watch, wait and rejoin at the next one.”
